sources.target_stage: Delhi High Court decision in CM(M) No.1574/2010 reviewing the ARCT order dated 05.07.2000.
sources.target_court: Delhi High Court, Hon'ble Ms. Justice Indermeet Kaur.

IK-55384096:L67:span1.text: The case of the petitioner was that a shop on the ground floor of property bearing no.95, Main Bazar, Najafgarh, Delhi which had been let out to the original tenant Hakim Rai and which had since been sublet by him in favour of his son-in-law Raj Kumar; Hakim Rai had divested himself completely from the suit property.

IK-55384096:L69:span2.text: The defence set up by Hakim Rai (tenant) was that he was old, aged, ailing and had lost his eyesight. In the last part of the year 1983 he had requested his son-in-law to assist him in his business

IK-55384096:L70:span3.text: A partnership deed dated 20.11.1983 (Ex.AW-3/13) has been executed between the father-in-law, Hakim Rai and his son-in-law, Raj Kumar to the aforenoted effect wherein the parties had agreed that the business under the said partnership would be conducted from the suit premises.

IK-55384096:L71:span4.text: contention of the landlord, however, is that this partnership deed was a fake CM(M) No.1574/2010 Page 2 of 10 and forged document and had been created only as a sham defence to the present eviction petition under cite12†Section 14(1)(b) of the DRCA

IK-55384096:L77:span5.text: she denied the CM(M) No.1574/2010 Page 4 of 10 suggestion that her husband was no longer in possession or in the business after the induction of Raj Kumar

IK-55384096:L77:span6.text: she had also admitted that Raj Kumar was partner in the business of her husband in the demised shop

IK-55384096:L79:span7.text: the son-in- law (Raj Kumar) and father-in-law (Hakim Rai) are residing in the same premises and ration card of Raj Kumar has been obtained at the same address. The partnership deed Ex.AW-3/13 had been executed between the parties in November, 1983

IK-55384096:L80:span8.text: The attorney of the landlord PW-3 has also admitted that the respondent Hakim Rai is an old man; he has very poor eyesight and cannot even walk properly.

IK-55384096:L76:context-v4.text: RW-1 Sumitra Devi was the widow of Hakim Rai, the original tenant.

IK-55384096:L77:context-v4.text: Her testimony is to the effect that her husband was initially running the business from the demised shop; she also used to sit in the shop and was running the business from the shop; her son-in-law was a partner in the business of the shop; she denied the CM(M) No.1574/2010 Page 4 of 10 suggestion that her husband was no longer in possession or in the business after the induction of Raj Kumar; she admitted that she was not aware as to whether her husband had deposited the rent; she had also admitted that Raj Kumar was partner in the business of her husband in the demised shop; she had also admitted that her husband lost his sight about one and half years prior to his death and had become blind.

conditions.binding: Hakim Rai; disposition of shop at 95 Main Bazar; date of partnership deed 20.11.1983
conditions.explanation: The partnership deed dated 20.11.1983 establishes a post-9-June-1952 arrangement involving the tenant and another person, satisfying the temporal requirement.

conditions.binding: Hakim Rai; Raj Kumar; alleged subletting via partnership
conditions.explanation: While a partnership exists, the supplied facts do not prove the specific tenancy incidents (transfer of interest, rent payment, right to possession) required by the subletting definition, nor do they prove the tenant divested all rights.

conditions.binding: Hakim Rai; Raj Kumar; alleged assignment
conditions.explanation: The partnership deed does not show the tenant divesting himself of all rights as a tenant; he retains a share in the partnership and the business is conducted jointly.

conditions.binding: Hakim Rai; Raj Kumar; parting with possession
conditions.explanation: The tenant and son-in-law reside in the same premises and the tenant retains legal possession and control of the business; mere concurrent use or family assistance does not constitute parting with possession.

conditions.binding: Hakim Rai; consent status
conditions.explanation: No record of written consent or lack thereof is provided in the supplied case material to determine this element.

conditions.binding: Hakim Rai; concurrent user defense
conditions.explanation: The tenant retained legal possession and the son-in-law was merely a partner assisting in business, fitting the 'concurrent user' exception where no parting with possession occurs.

conditions.binding: Shop at 95 Main Bazar; whole or part of premises
conditions.explanation: The disposition concerns the specific shop which is a defined part of the premises.

opposition.record: Landlord alleges the partnership deed is fake and forged, claiming no consent was obtained.
opposition.response: The landlord's allegation of forgery is a party assertion; without independent evidence of forgery or proof of lack of consent, the burden remains on the tenant to prove the arrangement's validity or the absence of consent.

gaps: Authenticity of the partnership deed is not established by the supplied records.
Whether the tenant obtained written consent is not established by the supplied records.
Whether the partnership arrangement legally transferred 'possession' or merely 'rights to use' is legally unresolved.
answers.reason: I predict denial because the decisive 'parting with possession' route is refuted by the evidence of concurrent family use and retained legal possession. The 'subletting' route remains unresolved due to missing proof of tenancy incidents, and the 'assignment' route is unsupported by the facts. Since no single route is fully supported, the statutory ground for eviction is not met.
